audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows contradict their reasons. whys[0] says 'you both just farm... concede nothing' under win[0]='Aurora'; whys[1] says 'you can trade up' under 'Skill'; whys[3] opens 'Even skirmish' under 'Irelia'. The packet levelChart and the already-applied mirror audit both read Skill / Irelia / Irelia / Skill / Aurora / Irelia / Irelia.
audit.why: Level 1 neither champion can commit; level 2 Irelia gets a second point while Aurora still cannot burst; levels 4-5 are a genuine coin-flip because Across the Veil breaks any chain.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1 and 3 flipped in both layers with matching ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why was the generic 'Vanguard's Edge walls off his disengage' line under a stage the chart correctly gives to Aurora, and no Aurora cooldown number appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Between Worlds is 140/120/100s — a 140-second rank-1 ultimate is a huge window whenever it is spent. Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s and is the escape that actually decides her engages, not Twofold Hex.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten from Riot's own description of Between Worlds; breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0] retargeted onto Across the Veil with its 22s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly told the player to tank Aurora's poke under Defiant Dance. Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage during the charge; Aurora's kit is magic damage, so it does nothing against her. That reversal was steering the player into the exact trades she wins. The full layer also tracked Twofold Hex (her 900-range poke) as 'her escape', which it is not — the escape is Across the Veil's leap into invisibility.
audit.why: Riot's text: Irelia W — 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Aurora W — 'leaps in a direction of her choosing, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible'. Aurora Q is a 900-range missile that curses and is recast to drag the curses back, so it hits twice.
audit.corrected: whys[1], phases[1].why, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[0] and dontsFull[0] rewritten. 'Passive shred' also corrected — Ionian Fervor is stacking attack speed plus on-hit at max stacks, not resist shred.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] was headed 'Build MR' with a body about passive stacks and Q-resets.
audit.why: Her whole kit is magic damage, so Mercury's Treads and Wit's End are the answer and Defiant Dance is not.

notes: Left alone as unverifiable: whys[4] and spikes[1] both say Between Worlds can 'pull and exile you out of position'. Riot's description only says she leaps, releases a damaging slowing shockwave, and creates a slowing area she can teleport across — no pull and no exile. I did not repeat that claim in anything I wrote, but it is still live in the content layer and should be checked. Also flagging that mid and late still tell the player Defiant Dance blunts her poke; I corrected the level-2 instance and the phase line, but those two long paragraphs carry the same reversal and need a hand pass. Anti-heal is worth stating somewhere: Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell and attack that damages you.
